mika (support): Hey team, seeing a support escalation from a large customer — they report intermittent 500s and long tail p99 latency from eu-west for our text-generation endpoint. Started ~08:20 UTC, affected ~8% of requests. :rotating_light:

sam (sre): can you paste logs / sample request ids? any client IPs?

mika (support): pasted a few request ids in the ticket. Quick sample curl from their host shows p95 ~320ms but p99 ~1.4s and some TLS handshake timeouts. They say it seems worse from their us-east infra via our eu-west pop.

jules (neteng): interesting — could be asymmetric egress path to our eu-west PoP or a cross-AS congestion lane. Can we get a traceroute from the customer?

mika (support): customer attached traceroute and tcpdump snippet. putting the relevant bits here:

mika (support): ```
traceroute to eu-west.redwood.example (35.187.12.34), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.0 ms
 2  93.184.216.1  12.4 ms  11.9 ms  12.0 ms
 3  185.60.21.10  28.3 ms  28.4 ms  28.2 ms
 4  * * *
 5  34.120.0.1  120.5 ms  121.0 ms  119.8 ms
 6  35.187.12.34  320.1 ms  319.9 ms  320.3 ms
```

mika (support): tcpdump shows several retransmits during handshake around hop 5-6.

jules (neteng): hop 5 looks like an upstream carrier or cloud egress AS — latency jump there. Could be transient congestion or path flap causing retransmits. Any BGP trace available?

tara (infra): I pulled our egress metrics for eu-west PoP at 08:15-08:30 UTC — small burst of retransmits on the fiber uplink to AS-XYZ and a slight increase in TLS handshake timeouts on one NIC. NIC didn't show errors at the host level though.

sam (sre): ok, so two potential contributors: customer path via their provider + our egress path exhibiting transient congestion. We should mitigate customer impact quickly: shift traffic off the affected egress path / PoP if possible.

leo (oncall): we can toggle egress affinity / prefer-alt-pop routing for that customer at the edge for a short window. I'll start an action.

deploy-bot: Deploy job 4827 queued by leo (oncall) — rolling traffic policy change to prefer eu-north for customer X.

sam (sre): while that's rolling, collect more data: tcpdump on our edge for those request ids, and netflow samples. Also capture SNI and TLS latency breakdown from the edge proxy.

tara (infra): capturing tcpdump now on lb-eu-west-03 and exporting to secure bucket. netflow shows around 6% packet loss to AS-XYZ in that window.

jules (neteng): I'm opening a ticket with upstream ASN and attaching the pcap + traceroute. Might be a persistent microburst or queueing on their peering link.

mika (support): customer confirmed immediate improvement after we toggled preference — p95 dropped to 65ms for a 10-minute test. They still want postmortem and a permanent fix.

sam (sre): good. Short-term mitigation worked. Next steps: 1) confirm if this is isolated to that upstream ASN, 2) decide on routing policy (per-tenant anycast steering or per-route blackhole/avoid), 3) add monitors for handshake retransmit ratio and cross-AS loss spikes.

jules (neteng): for (1) I'm seeing similar small spikes on a different tenant that rides the same egress. Not fully widespread, so likely upstream localized.

tara (infra): for (2) we can implement a per-customer egress override that pins to alternative PoPs for customers behind unstable carriers. It's quick but increases complexity. Maybe add to Dedicated offerings as an SLA feature.

sam (sre): agreed. For (3) I'll add a short-term synthetic probe that simulates TLS handshake + 1 token request from eu-west via multiple upstream AS paths and alert if p99 > 500ms or handshake retransmit ratio > 2%.

mika (support): customer asked for repro steps and evidence we engaged their provider. Jules, can you share the upstream ticket id so we can include in the support thread?

jules (neteng): opened ticket with ASN-XYZ: INC-7894, attached pcap and traceroute, asked for spool/queue stats for 08:10-08:40 UTC.

leo (oncall): note — we also observed a small config push to our eBPF offload on lb-eu-west-03 ~08:18 UTC. @tara was that a manual change? Could be correlated.

tara (infra): that was an automated kernel security patch that landed earlier in the maintenance window, but it shouldn't affect eBPF offload paths. I'm verifying.

sam (sre): please confirm the patch index and if any sockets were drained. If we can reproduce the load with a replay, we can rule in/out the patch.

tara (infra): kernel patch: 5.15.0-78 applied at 07:58 UTC to control plane nodes, no roll to edge LBs. Confirmed LB hosts weren't patched at that time.

jules (neteng): leaning heavily on upstream congestion. I've scheduled a call with ASN-XYZ NOC for 09:30 UTC to review.

mika (support): customer is satisfied for now but wants a timeline. We'll tell them we completed mitigation, opened upstream ticket INC-7894, and will follow up after NOC call + our postmortem.

sam (sre): action items assigned:
- jules: follow upstream ticket and post call notes (due 10:00 UTC)
- tara: validate LB kernel/eBPF state across eu-west fleet and attach netstats (due 09:00 UTC)
- leo: roll back traffic steering only after NOC confirms stable path and our probes green (monitoring will be green for 30m)
- sam: write a short postmortem draft and include synthetic metrics + pcap summary (due EOD)

deploy-bot: Deploy job 4827 succeeded — traffic policy change active.

mika (support): noted. I'll update the customer thread with mitigation steps and expected follow-up.

sam (sre): one more thing — add an automatic fallback policy for TLS handshakes that fail >2x: return 502 with Retry-After rather than retrying through the same path, to avoid amplification and head-of-line blocking for other requests.

jules (neteng): good idea. I'll propose an edge policy change in PR and mark it high priority.

mika (support): thanks all, will close customer alert once we get final confirmation from ASN-XYZ. :thumbsup:
